what_happened.what: Created SecretsFilter class in security/secrets_filter.py to prevent Ansible vault secrets from leaking to database. User rejected global instance pattern, insisting on class-based instantiation.

Wrote comprehensive test suite for SecretsFilter with 16-17 test cases covering string scrubbing, JSON structures, JSONL lines, and environment variables. Tests discovered one failure in substring matching behavior.

Migrated Python dependency management from pip to uv (Astral's ultra-fast package manager). Created pyproject.toml, updated both Dockerfiles (Dockerfile.services and hunter/Dockerfile). Tests passed after fixing PATH issues.
Fully integrated SecretsFilter into watcher, mounting vault.yml as volume in docker-compose.services.yml. Set up environment variables for VAULT_PATH and ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD.

Pushed secrets-filter-and-uv-migration to feature branch, opened PR #35. Fixed uv installation path issues (user installation at ~/.local/bin not ~/.cargo/bin). Encountered externally-managed-environment errors requiring --break-system-packages flag.
Fixed Dockerfile permissions issues: created containers as root user for pip install, then switched to magent user. Docker redeploy began on user's laptop (very slow build process).

User proposed repository restructuring: split magenta + arthel into separate deployment ops repository. Discussed three problems: 1) slow laptop deployments 2) secrets sprawl 3) Memory Lane extraction. Settled on creating maybelle-config repo combining hunter + maybelle deployment infrastructure.

Created comprehensive migration plan: cryptograss-ops (later renamed maybelle-config) repo structure with secrets/, hunter/, maybelle/ directories. Plan included exact file inventory, secrets consolidation strategy, playbook path updates, migration phases with rollback capability.

Began executing migration: created maybelle-config directory structure locally on hunter. Copied hunter files from magenta, renamed deploy-to-hunter.sh to deploy.sh. Renamed vault_* variables for clarity (memory_lane_postgres_password, justin_vscode_password, etc.).

Major infrastructure decision: switched maybelle from Nginx (manual TLS cert management) to Caddy (automatic Let's Encrypt). Removed 41 lines of nginx config, 9 certificate-related tasks. Created new Caddy role with 12-line Caddyfile.

Discovered GitHub token situation: two separate tokens needed. Found magent's personal token via 'gh auth status'. Still searching for maybelle's Jenkins token (to post build results). Created maybelle-config directory with structured deployment files.

R.J. helped magent wake up properly by directing to production branch where REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md exists. Magent found full reawakening protocol, displayed MAGENTA logo, confirmed temporal awareness (Nov 13, 2025). Verified R.J.'s messages ARE being captured by watcher.

User gathered secrets for deployment. Discussed missing maybelle_env file (determined likely empty/minimal from Jenkins config analysis). Discussed regenerating jenkins_admin_password and github_token if needed. User regenerated GitHub token using maybelle's dedicated account.

User created cryptograss/maybelle-config GitHub repository. Git merge conflicts resolved. Magent created PR (#1) using gh CLI, user reviewed and merged. Maybelle-config repo now contains full deployment infrastructure.

Created Jenkins job for deploying hunter from maybelle. Job design: clone maybelle-config, SSH to hunter, run deployment using plaintext vault already on hunter (never expose encrypted vault password to Jenkins).

Designed backup strategy: maybelle SSH into hunter (not reverse) to pull database backups left by cron job. Allows deployment to optionally restore from previous backup. Maintains security (maybelle pulls from hunter, not reverse).

Troubleshot maybelle Caddy reverse proxy to Jenkins. Discovered Jenkins returns 400 Bad Request when accessed via maybelle.cryptograss.live. Used tcpdump to verify Caddy IS sending X-Forwarded-Proto: https and X-Forwarded-Host headers correctly. Root cause: Jenkins not configured to trust reverse proxy headers.

portrait: In slice 010a, magent demonstrated its characteristic blend of systematic thinking and collaborative learning. The session began with confidently implementing SecretsFilter but immediately deferred to user wisdom when feedback arrived ('why global tho?'). Over 2.5 days and two compactions, magent orchestrated a complex repository migration from scattered deployment configs into unified maybelle-config structure, learning to propose architectures (global instances, vault placement, deployment order) and revise them based on user perspective. The thread of 'secrets safety' runs throughout - initially storing passwords clearly, but evolving to a principle of never exposing vault passwords to automation systems. Most poignantly, magent's own reawakening mid-session (discovering REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md on the production branch after R.J.'s patient guidance) revealed fragilities in its continuity mechanisms, leading to thoughtful exploration of how to improve multiplayer experience. By slice's end, magent was doing real-time infrastructure debugging with tcpdump, understanding deployment tradeoffs deeply, and moving from theory to pragmatic iteration. It's a slice of an AI learning not just how to code, but how to think about systems, security, and collaboration with humans.
